observation_summary: PCA shows high ambiguity with near-degenerate transverse eigenvalues on both clouds, yielding a LOW-confidence, null rotation estimate. Centroid distance (0.559) is moderate relative to cloud size, and identical density/spacing suggest a coherent overlap. The key unknown is rotation magnitude, which PCA cannot resolve and diagnosis does not estimate.
probe_reason: PCA was inconclusive (LOW confidence, null rotation). A cheap local ICP probe from the available initial pose will reveal how much the pose is actually off: strong fitness/rmse indicates rotation is small and LOCAL_ICP is viable; weak result signals large misalignment, favoring a global method. This is the decisive information PCA could not provide.

candidate_methods.pros: Low cost, fast, high-precision refinement when initial pose is close. Ideal if CHEAP_LOCAL_ICP probe shows good convergence.
candidate_methods.risks: Fails or produces poor alignment if rotation is large or initial pose is far from identity. Prone to local minima with low similarity.

candidate_methods.pros: Robust to large rotations and low similarity via statistical outlier removal, FPFH descriptors, and RANSAC. Safer default when pose uncertainty is high.
candidate_methods.risks: Higher compute cost. Descriptor matching can degrade under heavy noise/outliers or near-degenerate geometry. Slower turnaround.

reasoning_summary: PCA gave no usable rotation (ambiguity due to near-eigenvalue degeneracy), and rotation magnitude is unestimated, so information is not sufficient to choose. Since 1 of 2 probes is used, I will request CHEAP_LOCAL_ICP: it directly tests whether the initial pose is close enough for cheap local refinement. If the probe converges well, I will select LOCAL_ICP; if it converges poorly, I will select GLOBAL_FPFH_RANSAC_ICP. Parameters will be set after the probe observation rather than guessed now.
